module_title: Advanced System Commands and Developer Shortcuts
introduction: Tailored for SSC CGL Tier-2 (Mains) and IT Officer exams, this advanced module covers system-level Windows executions, permanent file deletion, and browser developer tools.

core_concepts.title: Windows Execution Shortcuts
core_concepts.description:
- `Win + R`: Open the 'Run' dialog box (used to execute system commands directly).
- `Win + E`: Open File Explorer (My Computer / This PC).
- `Win + I`: Open Windows Settings.
- `Win + X`: Open the Quick Link menu (the hidden advanced context menu over the Start button).

core_concepts.title: Permanent Deletion
core_concepts.description: - `Shift + Delete`: Delete the selected item permanently, completely bypassing the Recycle Bin.

core_concepts.title: Advanced Browser Shortcuts
core_concepts.description:
- `Ctrl + Shift + N`: Open a new Incognito/Private window (in Google Chrome).
- `Ctrl + Shift + Delete`: Open the 'Clear browsing data' dialog box (to delete cache/cookies).
- `F11`: Enter or exit Full-screen mode in a browser.

core_concepts.title: Developer Tools
core_concepts.description: - `F12` or `Ctrl + Shift + I`: Open the Developer Tools console (Inspect Element) in web browsers.

important_entities.name: Shift + Esc (Browser)
important_entities.significance: Pressing `Shift + Esc` inside Google Chrome opens Chrome's internal Task Manager, allowing you to see which specific tab or extension is consuming your RAM.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: While `Ctrl + Shift + N` opens an Incognito window in Chrome and Edge, if the exam specifically asks for **Mozilla Firefox**, the shortcut changes to `Ctrl + Shift + P` (Private window).
Many students guess that `Win + E` opens Microsoft Edge or Internet Explorer. This is strictly FALSE. `Win + E` stands for File **E**xplorer.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: R = Run, E = Explorer, X = eXpert Menu
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use these first letters to memorize the advanced Windows Key (`Win`) combos.

exam_strategy_tips: `Shift + Delete` is one of the most frequently asked questions in high-level computer awareness tests. Remember that it permanently removes the file without sending it to the Recycle Bin.
